title: Online convex optimization with exact separation and per-round query caps
summary: Expected regret for exactly feasible actions on an unknown convex body, with a separately enforced separation budget on each round.

description_paragraphs: Minimize adversarial online convex regret while maintaining exact feasibility in an unknown convex body under a strictly enforced separation-query cap on every round.
task.formulation: Minimize adversarial online convex regret while maintaining exact feasibility in an unknown convex body under a strictly enforced separation-query cap on every round.

description_paragraphs: The unknown compact convex body satisfies $rB_2^d\subseteq K\subseteq RB_2^d$ with public common center zero and public $0<r\le R$. Set $\kappa=R/r$; these supplied radii need not be optimal for the individual body.

After the current action, the convex loss may depend on the past and that action. A returned subgradient at the action has norm at most G. The guarantee is uniform over comparators and admissible adaptive loss sequences.

assumptions.description: The unknown compact convex body satisfies $rB_2^d\subseteq K\subseteq RB_2^d$ with public common center zero and public $0<r\le R$. Set $\kappa=R/r$; these supplied radii need not be optimal for the individual body.

assumptions.scope: The domain stated in this clause.

description_paragraphs: Before each action, at most Q calls to an exact strong separation oracle may be made. On any query z in the full Euclidean space, it returns inside if z belongs to K, or a unit vector a satisfying $\sup_{x\in K}\langle a,x\rangle<\langle a,z\rangle$. The oracle may choose any valid response.

The learner then plays $w_t\in K$ and receives the current convex loss and a subgradient $g_t\in\partial f_t(w_t)$ with $\|g_t\|\le G$. The upper algorithms use only the subgradient. All preprocessing access to K is charged from round 1; unused calls cannot be carried to a future round. Arithmetic and tests against explicitly stored inequalities are not unknown-body queries.

description_paragraphs: $R_T=\sup_{u\in K}\sum_{t=1}^T[f_t(w_t)-f_t(u)]$. The risk is the infimum over almost-surely feasible capped learners of worst-case expected regret over bodies, valid oracle responses, and admissible loss adversaries.
metric.base_expression: $R_T=\sup_{u\in K}\sum_{t=1}^T[f_t(w_t)-f_t(u)]$. The risk is the infimum over almost-surely feasible capped learners of worst-case expected regret over bodies, valid oracle responses, and admissible loss adversaries.

description_paragraphs: The resource is the joint pair (T,Q), where Q is a hard per-round cap rather than an average or total budget; total separation calls are at most QT. One loss/subgradient response is obtained after each action. Internal arithmetic, bit precision, and known-inequality processing are uncharged.

regimes.name: All asphericities with the specified logarithmic cap
regimes.predicate_text: $d,T\ge1$ integers, $G,R,r>0$, $r\le R$; fix $a>0$. The strict cap is either $Q=Q_*=2L_T$ or satisfies $L_T+1\le Q\le[\log(edT\kappa)]^a$ (when the latter interval is nonempty). All finite dimensions, including d=1. More generally the same logarithmic rate holds for $L_T+1\le Q\le[\log(edT\kappa)]^a$ for any fixed a>0 when this interval is nonempty; hidden logarithmic exponents may depend on a. This assertion does not include the literal cap Q=1 merely because one is bounded by a polylogarithm.
